title: Thermostat-style load probe for burst and steady throughput certification
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a repeatable, customer-facing notebook and test harness that can certify Dedicated capacity offers the contracted throughput guarantees across both burst and sustained windows. This work builds a thermostat-style probe that actively adjusts offered load to map capacity boundaries, validates autoscaler behavior under multi-tenant pressure, and produces an executable signoff artifact customers can run during onboarding.
goals: Deliver a reproducible test notebook that operators and customers can run to measure sustained and burst throughput against SLAs
Expose autoscaler hysteresis and cooldown behaviors so we can set safe defaults for Dedicated autoscaling policies
Produce a standardized acceptance report with measured percentiles, error rates, and capacity headroom for signoff
non_goals: Replace existing large-scale stress farms or long running soak tests
test_plan: The harness runs two phases per scenario: a burst probe (30s ramp, 90s peak, 60s cooldown) and a sustained probe (10m ramp, 30m sustain). For each run we capture per-request latency p50/p90/p95/p99, tail latency, token throughput, error types, and GPU utilization. We exercise model variants (fp16, 8-bit quantized) and common sequence lengths (64, 256, 512 tokens). The harness also injects synthetic tenant noise to validate QoS and tenant-aware fleet controls.
acceptance_criteria: Sustained throughput at contracted QPS for 30 minutes with p95 latency under 200ms for 256-token workload
Burst window recovers within configured cooldown with no more than 2% error rate increase
Autoscaler scales to required replica count within configured scale-up window and does not oscillate beyond two cycles
Generated customer report includes raw traces, aggregated percentile tables, and a pass/fail judgment that operators can sign
steps: Implement thermostat probe agent that increases offered QPS until latency breach or error threshold then backs off and records inflection points
Integrate tenant-noise simulator to mimic concurrent low-priority workloads
Wire probe into console dashboards and a lightweight report generator (PDF + JSON) for customer signoff
Add CLI/Notebook runner with configuration presets for common SKUs and sequence lengths
Write CI job that validates harness against staging Dedicated pool nightly
measurement_matrix: Capture metrics: request_latency_ms (p50,p90,p95,p99), token_throughput_per_second, errors_per_minute (4xx/5xx/timeout), gpu_utilization_percent, autoscaler_replica_count_over_time, kv_cache_hit_rate. Annotate runs with model, quantization, batch_size, and sequence_length.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We will limit run time for customer-facing signoffs to 40 minutes to balance confidence and cost; longer soak tests live in internal suites
Thermostat approach favors determinism over maximum peak discovery — it will find safe operating points customers can rely on rather than brittle maximums
We will not embed expensive cross-region failover tests in the initial notebook to reduce complexity; follow-ups can add multi-region scenarios
results_summary: Initial alpha runs against a 4-GPU Dedicated pool show thermostat inflection at 1.8x baseline QPS for 256-token workloads with p95 latency rising from 120ms to 210ms at the inflection point. Autoscaler scaled from 2->5 replicas within 45s on scale-up during a sustained ramp; no oscillation observed in 6 runs. Tenant-noise injection reduced available headroom by ~12% under realistic background load.
risks: Customer-run variability: network jitter or tenant-specific workloads may cause noisy results—report must include confidence boundaries
Cost: running the harness frequently against large pools is expensive; include cost estimate in onboarding docs
False negatives: misconfigured client-side batching can underreport capacity — include preflight checks
